sentence: Wir könnten montags joggen gehen.
tip: Put 'könnten' in position 2 and the infinitives 'joggen gehen' at the end.
translation_en: We could go jogging on Mondays.

sentence: Welche Sportart sollte ich machen?
tip: Start with the question phrase 'Welche Sportart' followed by 'sollte'.
translation_en: Which type of sport should I do?

sentence: Der Mann möchte gerne abnehmen.
tip: Put the modal verb 'möchte' in position 2 and 'abnehmen' at the end.
translation_en: The man would like to lose weight.

sentence: Die Frau arbeitet als Trainerin.
tip: Use 'arbeitet als' to state someone's profession.
translation_en: The woman works as a trainer.

sentence: Zwei Kilometer sind nicht so viel.
tip: The subject 'Zwei Kilometer' takes the plural verb 'sind'.
translation_en: Two kilometers are not that much.

sentence: Er braucht jetzt eine Pause.
tip: Place the time adverb 'jetzt' after the conjugated verb 'braucht'.
translation_en: He needs a break now.

sentence: Ich bin in einem Sportverein.
tip: Use the dative article 'einem' after 'in' for location.
translation_en: I am in a sports club.

sentence: Du solltest weniger Computerspiele spielen.
tip: Put 'solltest' in position 2 and the infinitive 'spielen' at the end.
translation_en: You should play fewer computer games.

sentence: Ich möchte immer sofort abwaschen.
tip: Separable verb 'abwaschen' stays together in the infinitive at the end.
translation_en: I want to always wash the dishes immediately.

sentence: Wir sollten mehr Fahrrad fahren.
tip: Place 'sollten' in position 2 and 'Fahrrad fahren' at the end.
translation_en: We should ride our bikes more.

sentence: Ich will meine Post gleich öffnen.
tip: Put 'will' in position 2 and 'öffnen' at the very end.
translation_en: I want to open my mail right away.

sentence: Du solltest deine Post sofort bearbeiten.
tip: Put 'solltest' in position 2 and 'bearbeiten' at the end.
translation_en: You should process your mail immediately.

sentence: Was nehmen Sie sich immer wieder vor?
tip: The separable prefix 'vor' goes to the very end of the question.
translation_en: What do you keep resolving to do?

sentence: Ich nehme mir vor, mehr Sport zu machen.
tip: Use an infinitive clause with 'zu machen' at the end.
translation_en: I resolve to do more sports.

sentence: Leider schaffe ich es oft nicht.
tip: Invert the subject and verb ('schaffe ich') because 'Leider' is in position 1.
translation_en: Unfortunately I often don't manage it.

sentence: Mein innerer Schweinehund ist zu groß.
tip: 'Mein innerer Schweinehund' is the subject in position 1.
translation_en: My lack of willpower is too big.

sentence: Warum laufen die Personen zusammen?
tip: Question word 'Warum' in position 1 followed by 'laufen'.
translation_en: Why are the people running together?

sentence: Du könntest im Park trainieren.
tip: Put 'könntest' in position 2 and 'trainieren' at the end.
translation_en: You could work out in the park.

sentence: Er trainiert viel im Fitness-Studio.
tip: Put the place 'im Fitness-Studio' after 'viel'.
translation_en: He works out a lot at the gym.

sentence: Am meisten trainiert er im Fußball-Club.
tip: Keep the verb 'trainiert' in position 2 after 'Am meisten'.
translation_en: He works out the most at the soccer club.

sentence: Wir könnten heute Abend gesund kochen.
tip: Time expression 'heute Abend' comes before manner 'gesund'.
translation_en: We could cook a healthy meal tonight.

sentence: Sie kann sehr gut Fisch mit Gemüse kochen.
tip: Put the infinitive 'kochen' at the very end of the clause.
translation_en: She can cook fish with vegetables very well.

sentence: Ihr solltet am Wochenende spazieren gehen.
tip: Put 'spazieren gehen' at the end of the sentence.
translation_en: You should go for a walk on the weekend.

sentence: Er joggt immer ohne sein Handy.
tip: The preposition 'ohne' is followed by 'sein Handy'.
translation_en: He always jogs without his phone.

sentence: Ich gehe oft mit meiner Oma spazieren.
tip: The verb 'spazieren' stands at the end of the sentence.
translation_en: I often go for a walk with my grandma.

sentence: Könnten wir am Dienstag schwimmen gehen?
tip: Start the yes/no question with the Konjunktiv II verb 'Könnten'.
translation_en: Could we go swimming on Tuesday?

sentence: Du solltest nicht so viel arbeiten.
tip: Put 'arbeiten' in the infinitive at the end.
translation_en: You shouldn't work so much.

sentence: Im Forum gibt es gute Ratschläge.
tip: Use the inverted structure 'gibt es' after 'Im Forum'.
translation_en: There are good pieces of advice in the forum.

sentence: Welche Tipps hast du zum Abnehmen?
tip: Start with the question phrase 'Welche Tipps'.
translation_en: What tips do you have for losing weight?

sentence: Freitags spiele ich immer Fußball im Verein.
tip: Fronting 'Freitags' puts the verb 'spiele' right before 'ich'.
translation_en: On Fridays I always play soccer at the club.

sentence: Du könntest mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit fahren.
tip: Place 'mit dem Fahrrad' before the destination 'zur Arbeit'.
translation_en: You could ride your bike to work.

sentence: Sollte ich lieber morgens oder abends laufen?
tip: Start the question with 'Sollte' and end with 'laufen'.
translation_en: Should I rather run in the morning or in the evening?

sentence: Wir nehmen uns für dieses Jahr viel vor.
tip: Place the separable prefix 'vor' at the end.
translation_en: We are resolving to do a lot for this year.

sentence: Nach dem Training bin ich immer müde.
tip: Put 'bin' in position 2 after 'Nach dem Training'.
translation_en: After the workout I am always tired.

sentence: Ein guter Trainer hilft dir beim Training.
tip: The verb 'hilft' takes the dative pronoun 'dir'.
translation_en: A good trainer helps you with your workout.
